content.value_statement: API teams need accurate documentation that stays close to code behavior. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code turn routes, schemas, examples, and error flows into usable API docs.
actual_capabilities: Documents REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket API patterns from provided code or route details.
Creates endpoint descriptions with methods, paths, authentication, parameters, request bodies, responses, and error cases.
Produces example requests for cURL, JavaScript, Python, and other requested languages.
Suggests OpenAPI or Swagger structures and Postman collection content.
Adds usage guidance for authentication, pagination, rate limits, filtering, sorting, and troubleshooting.
limitations: It depends on accurate source code, route definitions, schemas, or examples supplied in the conversation.
It cannot verify live endpoint behavior unless the environment and permissions allow tests.
Generated OpenAPI or Postman content still needs project-specific validation.
It may miss hidden behavior that is not visible in the provided code.

use_cases.title: Document a new API release
use_cases.description: Turn route handlers, schema files, and controller logic into endpoint docs before release.

use_cases.title: Create external developer guides
use_cases.description: Convert technical API details into clear onboarding docs with examples and error handling.

use_cases.title: Compare docs with expected behavior
use_cases.description: Use generated request, response, and error sections as review material for test planning.

prompt_templates.title: Document One Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single route or handler.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this route description to create developer-ready API documentation. Include method, path, authentication, parameters, request body, responses, errors, and examples: [paste endpoint details].

prompt_templates.title: Build REST API Reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a small REST service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these routes and models. Create a grouped REST API reference with overview, authentication, endpoints, data models, errors, pagination, and rate limits: [paste files or summaries].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare OpenAPI Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this API implementation and produce OpenAPI-ready notes. Include operations, schemas, security requirements, example values, and unresolved questions: [paste code].

prompt_templates.title: Review Docs Against Code
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for release documentation review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these existing API docs with the current implementation. Identify mismatches, missing endpoints, outdated examples, and changes needed before publication: [paste docs and code].

output_examples.input: A route file for creating users with validation and authentication rules.
output: Endpoint section for Create User with method, path, authentication, body fields, success response, error responses, and example requests.
Notes for validation constraints, duplicate email behavior, and missing token handling.

output_examples.input: A GraphQL user query and resolver summary.
output_examples.output: A GraphQL reference section explaining query purpose, variables, returned fields, permission rules, and common errors.

output_examples.input: Existing docs and updated API code before a release.
output_examples.output: A review list of mismatched paths, missing response fields, outdated examples, and documentation updates required before publishing.

best_practices: Provide route files, schema definitions, authentication rules, and known error cases together.
Ask for examples in the languages your API users actually use.
Validate generated docs against tests, live sandbox behavior, or an OpenAPI validator.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent endpoints that are not present in the source.
Do not publish generated examples before testing them with valid credentials or sample tokens.
Do not omit authentication, rate limits, pagination, or error behavior from the input context.

faq.question: Can it generate OpenAPI documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce OpenAPI-ready notes and structures from provided routes, schemas, and examples.

faq.question: Does it call my API?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes how to create docs. It only tests endpoints if you provide tools and permission.

faq.question: Which API styles does it support?
faq.answer: It supports REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket APIs when the relevant implementation details are available.

faq.question: Can it update existing docs?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current documentation and code so it can identify gaps and outdated sections.

faq.question: Will it find every endpoint automatically?
faq.answer: Only if those endpoints are visible in the files, route summaries, or context you provide.

faq.question: Is the output ready to publish?
faq.answer: Review it first. Validate examples, authentication details, response formats, and generated specifications before publishing.
